citations.claim: Light body whipped to high speed at first violating step, showing close slingshot regime
Light body speed jumped from initial 10 to ~14.5 at pericenter approach
One step before violation momentum was still conserved and speed was lower

counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.03333 to 0.001 with all else identical; finer integration removes the momentum drift, confirming large-dt substepping cause.

explanation: Fast light body (m=1, vx=10) slingshots past heavy body (m=20) reaching ~14.5 speed by step 10 at distance ~1.27. Step 9 conserves momentum exactly (px=10) with 29 substeps, but step 10 with 31 substeps jumps px to ~10.07, violating momentum by 0.078 vs 0.02 allowed. Likely cause: fixed-dt outer step with adaptive substep controller uses non-momentum-conserving or asymmetric force evaluation under strong acceleration/fast motion, so close high-velocity encounter breaks exact momentum conservation. Finer dt removes it.
vision_note: The small blue body travels quickly from the left toward the larger blue body, closing the gap steadily across steps 7 to 9 as shown by its dotted trail. By step 10 it arrives in a very close near-grazing encounter almost touching the larger body.
